C caps a processed input line at MAX_INPUT_LENGTH-1 = 255 kept bytes (each '$' costs 2 for its doubling, a backspace restores its cost, non-printables are skipped) and, when the budget runs out with input remaining, first writes "Line too long.  Truncated to:\r\n<processed prefix>\r\n" and then runs the prefix. The port truncates at TerminalLine and sends the same notice ahead of the cut command, covering the telnet and WebSocket paths; the 1024-byte raw-read cap remains as a safety net above the 255 rule.
